why: I judged Q on the MAIN table of SCRIPT_FINAL.md v6.3 (14 spoken beats), not the TRIAL variant. All three sit in the ordinary-good band and none is a clear 7. Q edges ahead because it opens on the finding rather than the failure, and that is the set the 19 Nov tease promised. It also explains the mechanism in plain words (seventeen joints, one dip per rep, my best rep not a textbook, a second pair of eyes), pays off concretely (chest fly continue, reverse crunch stop, half reps) and has the most shareable line. Its costs are an overclaiming hook, a label-reading cadence unlike Ep 2, and no spoken Gym Jarvis. P and R share the Ep 2 skeleton (research, tool plus two agents, guardrail, 'except this one', fix), which builders will like, but the hook sells a false alarm and the wave and agent wording loses mass viewers. P beats R because it closes the loop with a reason that checks out (worst rep 53 degrees against 122 best, so under half) and has a share line. R sounds most like the creator, with Ep 2's connectives and 'isn't allowed' echo, and has the cleanest mechanism order, but it ends on 'which was fair' and asks the viewer for nothing. The best version would be Q's hook (softened) and payoff in R's voice, with P's 'under half my best' line. Every spoken claim in all three checks against facts.md, apart from Q's hook wording.
